Wipro, HCL Tech, Coforge, and Persistent Systems gained up to 2% after the opening bell.Artificial intelligence-linked stocks plunged on fears of tougher AI regulation after Democrats won ‌control of the US Congress, defeating President Donald Trump’s Republican Party in the midterm elections. Democrats’ victory sparked concerns that tighter regulation could slow the AI infrastructure buildout that has helped lift stocks to record highs this year.Nasdaq fell 6%, marking its worst drop since the infamous Covid-19 crash in March 2020. The tech-heavy index also entered a technical ‘correction’ territory, a 10% drop from ⁠its October 6 record-high close.Nvidia shares plunged more than 9%, while the Philadelphia SE Semiconductor index crashed over 12%. The selloff wiped off $3 trillion in stock market value from S&P 500 companies. South Korea’s Kospi, which was seen as the face of the sharp volatility around the AI frenzy, also felt the pain, crashing more than 9% to trigger a circuit breaker.Also read | US stocks suffer worst rout since 2020: Dow plunges 1,800 points, Nasdaq crashes 5.5% as AI fears wipe out $3 trillion"Investors appear to be recognizing that some newly elected members of Congress and governors are looking to slow the pace of AI infrastructure development," Reuters quoted Melissa Brown, global head of investment decision research at SimCorp."While it seems unlikely that they will be able to stop it altogether, any slowdown would raise concerns because the AI growth story has largely depended on the rapid buildout of supporting infrastructure,” she said.Why Indian IT stocks stand to benefitEarlier this year, when Anthropic’s launch of new plugins for Claude triggered sharp hopes for artificial intelligence, India’s much-touted IT services companies saw a massive rout in their share prices as analysts worried that innovations could lead to displacement in the sector. "We call it the ‘SaaSpocalypse,’ an apocalypse for software-as-a-service stocks," Bloomberg quoted Jeffrey Favuzza from the equity trading desk at Jefferies as saying.However, as the AI frenzy began to fizzle out, analysts were quick to point out India’s so-called ‘anti-AI’ advantage. This has been boosting a recovery in these stocks while experts scream about a bubble-burst crisis ahead amid the massive spending behind AI infrastructure. Michael Burry, popular for correctly predicting the 2008 housing crisis, has been ramping up his warnings over the excessive optimism regarding AI. Recently, he said that the market is currently in a 'denial' mood, a phase that could last six to nine months as seen during the previous 2000 and 2008 crises.Also read | AI bubble is coming, and there is no way out! Aswath Damodaran explains what investors should do before the crash beginsAmid the growing concerns over the excessive frenzy around artificial intelligence, valuation expert Ashwath Damodaran said in a recent podcast that the AI bubble is coming and there is no way one can avoid it completely.These rising worries around the AI bubble will likely be a positive for Indian IT companies. Veteran banker Uday Kotak expects India to benefit from the reverse flows as the AI frenzy fizzles out, while working down the path of building its own AI capabilities. articles.title: Nithya Raman elected Mayor of Los Angeles
articles.summary: New York: Indian-born democratic socialist Nithya Raman has been elected Mayor of Los Angeles, scripting history as she becomes the first South Asian mayor of the nation's second-largest city.Raman, 45, who was a Los Angeles City Council member, defeated incumbent 73-year-old Karen Bass in the November 3 mid-term elections.Also read: Democrats' US midterm sweep may give India more room to negotiate a balanced trade deal with TrumpWith this victory, America's two largest cities - New York and Los Angeles - are now run by Indian-descent mayors who are Democratic Socialists."Los Angeles, I am deeply honoured to be your next Mayor. Thank you to the thousands of people who knocked on doors, sent texts, made phone calls, convinced their neighbours to believe in the promise of this big, beautiful, joyful city that we get to call home," Raman said in a video posted on X Thursday.Raman paid tribute to her predecessor Bass, the first woman mayor of Los Angeles, for her decades-long public service."I am going to City Hall to work every single day to earn your trust and to earn your trust in this city again. And that work starts now, so that we can build housing that people can afford, parks for our children to play in, a transit system that can get people where they need to go, a city that is safe for its working people and its families, and a city government that is actually capable of delivering on its promises," Raman said.LA City Councilmember for District 4, Kerala-born Raman is an urban planner by training, and she received her bachelor's degree from Harvard and a graduate degree from MIT.Raman is among the several Indian-American candidates who have emerged victorious across the country in the US midterm elections that concluded Tuesday and delivered a significant rebuke to President Donald Trump and the Republicans as the Democrats gained control of the House and Senate, flipping seats and traditional party strongholds in a massive blue wave across America.Also read: Marco Rubio weighs leaving administration after GOP’s midterm lossIndian American Impact, an organisation that empowers South Asian and Indian-American communities through community engagement, civic partnerships, and candidate support, congratulated Raman on her victory in the general election for Mayor of Los Angeles.Noting that Raman will become the first South Asian American mayor of the nation's second-largest city, the Indian American Impact said her victory reflects the growing political power of South Asian Americans in California, a state with more than one million South Asian residents, the largest such population in the country.Executive Director of Indian American Impact Chintan Patel said in a statement that Raman ran on lowering rents, building housing faster, and making city services work for Angelenos, and voters chose her to deliver it."With her win, South Asian Americans will lead the two largest cities in the United States," Patel said, referring to New York and its Mayor Mamdani.The 5.5 million-strong Indian-American community registered significant political gains in the midterms, with several candidates from the community winning historic elections to various positions across the country.Pia Dandiya of Florida and Dr Amish Shah of Arizona will be the newest Indian-American members of the US Congress, with their victories speaking to the "growing political power of our communities."They will join Representative Ami Bera, Representative Pramila Jayapal, Representative Ro Khanna and Representative Suhas Subramanyam at Capitol Hill."At a time of rising hate against our communities, representation matters, and they will fight to keep our communities safe," Indian American Impact said. "All six are committed to lowering costs for working families, expanding access to health care, and protecting immigrants, and they will serve as a powerful check on the Trump administration in the next Congress," the organisation said.Among the other notable election victories are that of Manoj Chourasia, who has been reelected to the New Hampshire State House, Darshana Patel who won her reelection to the California State Assembly, Ranjeev Puri whose won reelection to the Michigan House of Representatives.With Democrats retaking the chamber, Puri is expected to become Michigan's next Speaker of the House, which would make him the first Indian American Speaker of a state House in the country.Dr Krish Subrahmanian won his election for the Minnesota State Senate; Aruna Miller has been reelected as Lieutenant Governor of Maryland; Lisa Kaul won her election for the New York State Senate, defeating a Republican incumbent and flipping a seat in New York; and Nabeela Syed won her election for Illinois State Senate District 26.Amar Mukunda won his election to the Maryland State Senate; Saba Haider has been elected to the Illinois State House; Josh Kaul has been re-elected as Wisconsin's Attorney General; Pooja Sethi won her election to the Texas House, District 47, becoming the first Indian American to serve in the Texas legislature; and Jyot Singh has been elected to the Georgia State House, District 97, the first Indian American and first Sikh American elected to the Georgia State Legislature.

M-cap of BSE-listed companies tops Rs 500 lakh crore mark
articles.summary: Mumbai: The combined market capitalisation of all companies listed on the BSE crossed ₹500 lakh crore for the first time Thursday, reaching around ₹502 lakh crore ($5.31 trillion) amid a broad-based rally in equities and a steady addition of newly listed companies.It took 622 trading sessions for the total mcap to rise from ₹400 lakh crore, first crossed on April 8, 2024, to the latest milestone. The mcap first crossed ₹100 lakh crore on March 12, 2014, and took 1,494 sessions to reach ₹200 lakh crore on February 4, 2021. The ₹300 lakh crore milestone was reached on July 6, 2023, after another 586 sessions, while the subsequent rise to ₹400 lakh crore took 181 sessions.135589318The latest milestone is significant because it comes even as the benchmark Sensex and several broader market indices remain below their record highs. The Sensex is still 7.6% below its peak of 85,836, recorded on September 26, 2024.The BSE MidCap 150 is 5.3% below its record of 17,373, reached on August 26, 2026, while the BSE SmallCap 250 is 8.4% below its peak of 7,514, recorded on September 23, 2024. The BSE MicroCap 250 is 7% below its record of 19,988, reached on September 8, 2026.Read more: Why Nithin Kamath believes NRI investing in India has become easier than everA steady stream of initial public offerings (IPOs) has also contributed to the expansion of the overall mcap, even as several benchmark indices remain below their peaks. In 2024, 94 companies made their mainboard debut, adding around ₹12 lakh crore to mcap on their listing days. In 2025, 115 companies listed, adding nearly ₹14 lakh crore, while 107 companies have listed so far in 2026, adding above ₹25 lakh crore."The large number of IPOs has added to the overall mcap. At the same time, several companies outside the main indices have participated in the rally, helping total mcap reach a record even as major indices remain below their peaks," said Ankur Punj, MD, Equirus Wealth.The latest milestone has also coincided with a sharp recovery in equities. The Sensex and Nifty have gained more than 8.1% each in six consecutive sessions. The BSE MidCap 150 has advanced over 8.4% in eight of the past nine sessions, while the BSE SmallCap 250 has risen around 7% in seven of past eight sessions.Read more: Titan Q2 Results: Profit jumps 54% YoY to Rs 1,722 crore; total income up 25%The rally has been supported by a decline of more than 19% in crude oil prices over the past three sessions, easing concerns over inflation, India's import bill and the rupee. Strong foreign portfolio investor (FPI) buying, with net inflows of over $3.4 billion in the past 12 sessions, positive global cues, reduced uncertainty following the US midterm elections and better-than-expected second-quarter earnings have also lifted investor sentiment."The momentum could continue in the near term if crude prices remain stable at lower levels and foreign inflows sustain. However, investors should remain cautious as geopolitical developments, crude price volatility and profit booking after the sharp rally could limit further upside," said Ravi Singh, chief research officer at Master Capital Services.

articles.title: Demat account additions hit 9-month high in October as IPO boom draws investors
articles.summary: Mumbai: New demat account additions rose to a nine-month high in October, marking the fourth monthly increase in five months after a prolonged period of moderation between January 2025 and May 2026, as robust IPO activity drew more investors to the stock market.NSDL and CDSL together added nearly 3.36 million demat accounts in October, the highest monthly addition since January 2026. The total number of demat accounts stood at around 244 million at the end of the month. The number of demat accounts does not represent unique investors, as individuals can hold multiple accounts. The number of unique investors is estimated at around 136.6 million as of September, according to NSE data.Robust primary market activity was a key driver of the increase, with several large and smaller public issues attracting retail participation. October was the busiest month for IPO activity in 2026, with 13 issues raising a record ₹44,507 crore, including the Jio Platforms IPO - India's biggest ever.Read more: Why Nithin Kamath believes NRI investing in India has become easier than ever"Demat account openings typically rise when there is a surge in IPO activity, as investors open accounts to participate in public issues. The recent listing activity, including the large Jio Platform IPO and several smaller issues, has contributed to the increase," said Sunny Agrawal, head of fundamental equity research at SBICAPS Securities.Growing interest in gold and silver exchange-traded funds (ETFs) has also encouraged retail investors to open demat accounts, Agrawal said. Investors can purchase these products through the secondary market using a demat account.Read more: Equity mutual fund inflows may drop 18% in October as midcap and hybrid funds lose momentum: NomuraThe pickup in demat account additions came with gains in benchmark indices, with the Sensex rising 2% and the Nifty gaining 1.9% in October. However, broader market segments, which see greater retail participation, underperformed.

articles.title: Fed's Beth Hammack and Thomas Barkin favour gradual rate hikes as inflation stays high
articles.summary: Federal Reserve officials Beth Hammack and Thomas Barkin are making the case for a gradual approach to interest rate increases, signalling that policymakers remain focused on bringing inflation under control even as uncertainty over the economic outlook grows, Reuters reported.Their comments on Thursday come as the US central bank faces competing pressures from persistent price increases, geopolitical tensions and heavy investment in artificial intelligence (AI). The remarks also mark the first round of comments from Fed officials after Democrats won control of Congress and made gains in state level elections. For live updates on US Markets, click here "I expect that monetary policy will need to move to a restrictive stance to bring inflation back to 2% in a timely manner," Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland President Beth Hammack said in a speech ahead of an event in Zurich.According to Reuters, Hammack, a consistent supporter of higher borrowing costs, favours smaller and more frequent adjustments rather than sharp increases. She said this approach would be less disruptive to households, businesses and financial markets. Gradual increases could also prevent an “inflationary mindset” from taking hold, she added.Richmond Fed President Thomas Barkin echoed that view, saying inflation remained “too high” and was holding firm rather than easing. "When it comes to the pace of future rate hikes, gradual makes sense," he said.Inflation keeps pressure on the FedThe comments follow the Fed's decision last week to keep its benchmark interest rate in the 3.75%-4.00% range. Hammack, along with Fed Governor Lisa Cook, voted in favour of a rate increase, highlighting the divide among policymakers over how aggressively to tackle inflation.Also Read: Emerging markets lose $33.8 billion in October as investors flee Asian stocksFinancial markets broadly expect another increase in December, although expectations beyond that remain less certain. Reuters reported that futures traders have lowered the probability of a December hike to around 70% from more than 80% on Wednesday.AI investment and elections add to uncertaintyThe political shift could also influence the inflation outlook. Local voter opposition to data centres and permitting challenges could slow AI infrastructure spending, potentially easing demand for equipment and related resources.Evercore ISI analysts told clients on Wednesday that AI capital expenditure could slow in the next year or two, helping keep demand and supply in balance without requiring many more rate increases.TD Securities said it expects the Fed to raise rates by another 50 basis points by early next year. However, the brokerage said a resolution to the Iran war or a slowdown in AI investment could reduce the need for further tightening after March.Meanwhile, Friday's US jobs report is expected to provide another test for policymakers, with economists forecasting 65,000 additional jobs in October after September's 29,000 gain, Reuters reported.(Disclaimer: This article is based on inputs from agencies. These do not represent the views of The Economic Times)

articles.title: LTCG cut may come with a separate tax tweak
articles.summary: New Delhi/Mumbai: Key stakeholders are offering divergent prescriptions on how to address concerns over long-term capital gains tax (LTCG) tax and securities transaction tax (STT).These include scrapping LTCG altogether, removing it just for foreign portfolio investors (FPIs), or lowering the rate. As for STT, suggestions include reducing it for some products and increasing it for others, people familiar with the discussions said."A well thought-out call would be taken," said an official. Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman has said she will consider investors' concerns regarding LTCG. These measures are being considered as a way of stemming the exodus of overseas investors that has led to a slump in Indian stock markets.While the LTCG collections amounted to ₹1.29 lakh crore in FY25, those for STT stood at ₹57,522 crore. Any call on the levies would have to take into account the revenue impact and funding for social sector schemes and subsidies.Finance ministry officials have met senior market participants to seek their views on capital market taxation. ET had reported on October 28 that the finance ministry officials had reached out to stakeholders on the issue.Financial sector regulators including the Reserve Bank of India and the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) are understood to have backed the idea of doing away with LTCG to make India an attractive destination for foreign investors.Most participants favoured abolishing LTCG on equities while suggesting that the government could consider a marginal increase in STT on options trading alone, leaving cash and futures transactions untouched. They argued that options account for the bulk of daily trading activity and have been the focus of regulatory efforts to curb excessive speculation, people said.Some participants have cautioned against extending preferential tax treatment to FPIs alone, saying such a move could draw criticism from domestic investors. Short-term capital gains on listed equities, held for up to one year, are currently taxed at 20%, while long-term gains on holdings exceeding one year attract a 12.5% levy.Foreign portfolio investors have argued that several competing markets in the region do not levy LTCG, putting India at a disadvantage.Market participants said the combination of rupee depreciation and capital gains taxation has weighed on foreign investors' dollar-denominated post-tax returns, making other markets more attractive. One of the suggestions that has been put forth is calculating an FPI's taxable capital gains in dollar terms rather than rupees, said one of the persons.Separately, some FPI representatives also sought simplification of procedures governing the inflow and repatriation of foreign capital, calling for easier processes to bring funds into India and take money out of the country. Market participants said senior finance ministry officials have patiently heard out their suggestions.Another official said the implications of all suggestions would be examined before a final decision is reached.

articles.title: Mehli Mistry challenges Tata Trust exit
articles.summary: Mumbai: Former Tata trustee Mehli Mistry has challenged his removal as a trustee of Bai Hirabai Jamsetji Bai Hirabai Charitable Institution (BHJTNCI), arguing that the decision was invalid and that some trustees who voted against his reappointment were themselves ineligible.In a series of rejoinders filed with the deputy charity commissioner for Greater Mumbai Region, Mistry has argued that the trust deed does not prescribe a fixed tenure for trustees or specify citizenship or tax residency as a qualification for trusteeship.He also accused Sir Dorabji Tata Trust (SDTT) of attempting to prevent scrutiny of alleged governance lapses, including commissions and financial benefits received by trustees. The matter has been adjourned to December 3. Challenging the recording of his cessation as a BHJTNCI trustee with effect from October 28, 2025, Mistry argued that neither the trust's 1913 will nor its 1923 trust deed prescribes a fixed tenure for trustees.The trust's position that his three-year term had expired relied on a 2022 circular and appointment letter, but neither of them can override the governing instruments, he argued.Citing Clause 23 of the deed, Mistry said vacancies arise on grounds including death, permanent residence outside the Bombay Presidency, insolvency, renunciation of faith and unfitness, but not on expiry of a fixed term. The codicil also says trustees "shall always be trustees," he added.Mistry argued that he is not a "tenure trustee" under Section 2(17A) introduced through an 2025 amendment and that Section 30A(1), therefore, does not apply to him. He also cited the trust's annexures, which allegedly show different renewal periods for other trustees, including about two years for Vijay Singh and less than two years for Venu Srinivasan."The trust cannot use Section 30A(1) as a sword to oust the objector on October 28, 2025, and, in the same breath, ignore that very provision when its own vice chairman (Singh) acted in breach of it on that very day. A party cannot approbate and reprobate," Mistry said in his submission.He also cited a resolution passed on October 17, 2024, at a joint meeting of SDTT and Sir Ratan Tata Trust trustees, shortly after Ratan Tata's death. The resolution provided for trustees to be reappointed on expiry of their terms without any limit on tenure, he said.The trust deliberately omitted it from its reply to his complaint, Mistry claimed.He urged the authority to reject BHJTNCI's change report against him as "illegal, non-est and contrary to the trust deed."According to Mistry, Circular Resolution No 671 of October 23, 2025, proposing his reappointment, was approved by Jehangir H C Jehangir and Darius Khambata but was not approved by Noel Tata, Venu Srinivasan and Vijay Singh. Jimmy Tata did not respond.He said the trust failed to follow the 2024 resolution's requirement of unanimous approval.In a 24-page rejoinder filed under Section 22 of the Maharashtra Public Trusts Act, 1950, Mistry also contested the trust's objections to his citizenship and tax residency, saying the will, codicil or trust deed does not prescribe these as criteria for trusteeship."If foreign citizenship and overseas residence are to be treated as relevant considerations, they must be examined in relation to the reporting trustee with equal rigour," he further said and alleged that Noel Tata, the current reporting trustee, is an Irish citizen, a UAE tax resident and a UAE Golden Visa holder.He sought an affidavit from Tata detailing his citizenship and tax residency history, including whether he has held a Swiss passport.

articles.title: RBI proposes ₹100 crore limit on bank loans for agri infrastructure
articles.summary:
The Reserve Bank on Thursday proposed that loans for agricultural infrastructure will be subject to an aggregate sanctioned limit of Rs 100 crore per borrower from the banking system.
As part of the ongoing effort towards consolidation of various instructions, the Reserve Bank of India said it has undertaken a review of the extant guidelines relating to Priority Sector Lending (PSL) and proposes to issue directions on the subject for different regulated entities, including commercial banks and regional rural banks.
A draft direction on commercial banks proposed an aggregate loan limit of Rs 4 crore per borrowing entity for crop loans, medium and long-term loans for agriculture and allied activities, as well as loans for pre- and post-harvest activities.
It also said: "Loans for agriculture infrastructure will be subject to an aggregate sanctioned limit of Rs 100 crore per borrower from the banking system."
